_comment: P05-01 — LOCAL SYNTHETIC SECURITY MASTER + GOVERNED MAPPING REGISTER (fixture).
⚠ P04 is a SPECIFICATION, not an implementation. Nothing here builds the security master.
These are synthetic fixture records shaped to the ACCEPTED P04 contract so that P05-01 can
exercise identity handling without inventing identity rules.
Authorities applied:
CS-1  canonical security ID: required, immutable, unique, program-internal
XI-1  FIGI/OpenFIGI authoritative; ISIN/CUSIP/SEDOL non-authoritative (OI-09)
MC-1  cardinality 1:N — one canonical issuer to N securities/listings (OI-08)
MC-2  canonical -> companyId is an N:1 projection, expected not an error
MC-6  '${sector}-H1' synthetic values are mapping TARGETS only, never modelled as entities
MP-1  every mapping traceable to source, method, version and approval
MP-2  mappingMethod enumerated; 'inferred from symbol' PROHIBITED (ADP-1)
ADP-7 mappings are effective-dated
The FIGI values below are SYNTHETIC and deliberately non-real. No provider is implied.
No credential, endpoint or entitlement appears anywhere in this file.
P05-02-B additions (BD-P05-02-07 — lifecycle-state coverage completion):
LC-1  lifecycle state is effective-dated; it is always as of a date
LC-2  a transition NEVER mutates the canonical security ID (CS-5)
LC-3  identity records are never deleted; a retired identity stays resolvable for PIT queries
LC-4  'merged' and 'superseded' REQUIRE a successor reference, itself effective-dated.
Carried here as `successorRef: {canonicalSecurityId, effective:{from,to}}`. No new link-type
vocabulary is invented — the relationship is already named by `lifecycleStatus`.
LC-6  a state is NEVER inferred from absence of data. Missing provider data is not a delisting.
The lifecycle vocabulary itself is UNCHANGED: active|suspended|delisted|merged|superseded.

securities._note: MC-1: same canonicalIssuerId as CS-LOCAL-0001 — one issuer, two securities.
LC-2: delisting changed state and relationships, never the immutable canonical ID.
FC-2 NEGATIVE FIXTURE: has NO FIGI. An unresolved FIGI is an explicit unresolved state — never a fallback.
FC-1 NEGATIVE FIXTURE: a real canonical security with NO mapping record. Resolution must FAIL EXPLICITLY - no coercion, no placeholder, no synthesised companyId, no null join key (ADP-2).

P05-02-B / LC-1, LC-2: temporarily halted — the identity is INTACT and remains resolvable. A halt changes STATE, never the immutable canonical ID, and is never inferred from absent market data (LC-6). Given its own canonical issuer so the existing MC-1 fixture shape (one issuer, two securities) is left untouched.

P05-02-B / LC-4: 'merged' REQUIRES a successor reference and the predecessor→successor link is itself effective-dated. LC-3: the predecessor is never deleted and stays resolvable for historical/PIT queries.
P05-02-B / LC-4: 'superseded' REQUIRES a successor reference; the link is effective-dated. LC-2: supersession changes state and relationships, never the immutable anchor.

P05-02-B: the SUCCESSOR of CS-LOCAL-0007 (the absorbing instrument in the corporate event). MC-2: it projects onto the SAME companyId as its predecessor — an expected N:1 projection, not an error. MC-4: the two remain DISTINCT securities.
P05-02-B: the SUCCESSOR of CS-LOCAL-0008. A successor is a NEW canonical identity; it never reuses or mutates the predecessor's immutable ID (CS-1, LC-2).

mappings._note: MC-6: 'technology-H1' is a synthetic mapping TARGET only, never modelled as an entity.
MC-2: two distinct canonical security IDs project onto ONE companyId — expected N:1, not an error. MC-4: they remain two distinct securities.
ADP-7: effective-dated. A query as of 2024-01-01 must NOT resolve this — deterministic fail-closed.
MP-5 NEGATIVE FIXTURE: low confidence and NO approval. Confidence never substitutes for approval — this mapping is unresolved until approved.
P05-02-B: a suspension does NOT close the mapping window. LC-3 — the identity remains resolvable; LC-6 — absent market data is never read as a lifecycle change.
P05-02-B / LC-3: the merged predecessor's mapping stays OPEN so a PIT query as of the observation instant still resolves. ED-5: closing it would rewrite history rather than add to it.
P05-02-B / MC-2: successor and predecessor project onto ONE companyId — an expected N:1 projection. MC-4: they remain two DISTINCT securities.
P05-02-B / LC-3: the superseded predecessor remains resolvable; the supersession is carried by lifecycleStatus plus successorRef, not by deleting the mapping.
P05-02-B / MC-2: the successor projects onto the same companyId as CS-LOCAL-0008.

negativeFixtures._note: FC-1 / FC-2 / MC-7: each must produce an EXPLICIT, deterministic, named failure. CS-LOCAL-UNMAPPED exists as a security but has no mapping record, so it exercises FC-1 rather than an unknown-security path. FC-5: none is reported as a quality state. FC-6: E1-E8 is unchanged; identity failure is not E1 and adds no class.

venues.name: Synthetic Operating Exchange
venues._note: VN-1: venue identity is MIC-based. VN-3: operating MIC and segment MIC are never interchangeable.
